headline: Single-cell and spatial resources integrate cell typing, CNV and methylation markers
label: Single Cell Computational Methods
summary: Single-cell and spatial tools now combine transcriptomic, CNV and methylation data to resolve malignant and cell-type identity across platforms.
synthesis: The shared thread is computational inference of cell identity and state from single-cell and spatial measurements, increasingly built on integrated multi-layer inputs. CATFISHR combines RNA-expression similarity, inferred CNV profiles and consensus cell typing to identify malignant cells, and CNVSIM builds an interpretable copy-number reference atlas of 112 CNV-defined cancer subtypes. CellMethMarker provides 347,514 de novo and 2.2M literature-derived DNA methylation markers for deconvolution, while Spatialsnake unifies Visium, Visium HD, Stereo-seq, Xenium and MERFISH outputs in one SpatialData/Snakemake workflow. Curated resources extend this infrastructure to markers, spatial regulon activity and subcellular transcript maps. What is new here is the convergence on reusable, cross-platform tooling and reference atlases, including WAGES, which maps WGD clonal fraction in bulk tumors from expression, informed by single-cell evidence of WGD subclones in non-WGD tumors.
